data.narrative:
Carbyon is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Hans De Neve that has raised €22.3M to date. The valuation framework references a comparison universe of nine peers in the Climate & Energy sector: one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is the applicable valuation approach here. Using total capital raised of $22M as a baseline value proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, this method implies a valuation of $45M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy peer set—while eight same-sector competitors exist, none met the thresholds for meaningful statistical triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $38M to $51M, with a median point of $45M. This range reflects approximately ±15% variance around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct same-stage comparables, which limits cross-validation of the step-up multiplier applied, and the sparse public market reference (single ticker), both of which constrain confidence in the range width. Additional data on recent Series A rounds within climate tech would narrow these bounds materially.
